issues.issue: The obligation is imposed on "EMC or MSMCH, as applicable," but the cost is allocated "at EMC's own expense," so the text makes EMC bear a cost of MSMCH's performance. Which party pays when MSMCH performs cannot be read off the words.

The paragraph recites that "the Master Servicer agrees that it will not" alter the MERS codes, yet the Master Servicer is not a party to this Agreement (see the preamble naming only EMC, MSMCH and the Purchaser). Whether that undertaking binds anyone here is left open.

The due diligence obligation is measured by "such due diligence as any such party reasonably believes is appropriate," a standard set by the requesting party's own belief with no external benchmark. Its outer limit is not stated.

The paragraph imposes affirmative duties on the Trustee to assign loans and execute transfer instruments, but the Trustee is not a party to this Agreement under the preamble. Whether those duties are enforceable here, or only under the Pooling and Servicing Agreement, is a live question.

The text breaks off mid-sentence ("shall be submitted for recording ... at no expense to" followed immediately by "Certificates evidencing Percentage Interests aggregating not less than 25% of the Trust"), and the enumerated list contains two clauses numbered "(iv)." The recording exception cannot be applied as written.

The paragraph directs that on failure to record "the provisions of Section 5(c) and (d) shall apply," but Section 5 of this Agreement has only subsections (a) and (b), and "Material Defect" is defined nowhere in the instrument. The consequence of a recording failure therefore has no operative referent.
The final clause reads "and EMC not in default with respect to any order of any court," omitting the verb "is," so the sentence is ungrammatical as a warranty.

The warranty is given about "the Mortgage Loan Seller's Information (as defined in Section 14(a) hereof)," but Section 14(a) sets out closing conditions and defines no such term anywhere in the Agreement. The subject matter of this disclosure warranty is therefore unidentified.

EMC's only loan-level warranty appears here, yet no cure, repurchase or substitution remedy is provided for its breach — the remedy paragraph in Section 10 runs only against MSMCH, while Section 19 declares the Trustee's sole remedy to be obligations "contained in Sections 5 and 7," which contain none. What follows a breach by EMC cannot be determined from the instrument.

This warranty is given "with respect to each Mortgage Loan," including loans sold by EMC, while the remedy paragraph of Section 10 obliges MSMCH to cure, purchase or substitute only as to "MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans." Whether MSMCH warrants the whole pool, and with what consequence, is genuinely contestable.

The compliance warranty extends to "each Mortgage Loan," but the cure/repurchase machinery later in Section 10 is limited to MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans as defined in Section 1. The scope of MSMCH's exposure for EMC-sold loans cannot be settled without construing the two together.

"No Mortgage Loan is a High Cost Loan or Covered Loan, as applicable" leaves the qualifier "as applicable" without a referent, and the date formula "originated on or after October 1, 2002 through March 6, 2003" is awkwardly bounded. Both make the warranty's coverage uncertain at its edges.

The permitted-encumbrance list ends with the catch-all "other matters to which like properties are commonly subject which do not materially interfere with the benefits of the security," set against three specific enumerated exceptions. How far that residual category reaches is the sort of general-versus-specific question the words do not resolve.

The warranty turns on the Mortgage containing "customary and enforceable provisions such as to render the rights and remedies of the holder thereof adequate," a standard whose content ("customary," "adequate") is nowhere fixed. Whether a given form of mortgage satisfies it is not answerable from the text.

The sentence "unless at the time of the ... origination, such Mortgagor did not qualify taking into such facts as, without limitation, ..." omits a word (plainly "account") and the qualification test it states cannot be parsed. The warranty's condition is unintelligible as written.

This warranty is given "solely with respect to the Fremont Mortgage Loans ... and Accredited Mortgage Loans," yet subsection (b) in which it sits is expressly limited to MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans, a defined class that excludes Fremont and Accredited originations. The two cannot be harmonised without deciding which controls.

The warranty requires the appraiser to have been "duly appointed by MSMCH," but the MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans are by definition loans originated by third parties whose appraisers MSMCH did not appoint. The representation cannot be true as literally worded for the class it covers.

"LTV" is used without definition in this Agreement; the attached Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement defines "Loan-to-Value Ratio" by a formula that itself turns on a choice between appraised value and purchase price. How the 100% test is computed is therefore unfixed.

The paragraph deems the Section 10 warranties to be remade "by the related Mortgage Loan Seller" on substitution, although Section 10 contains only MSMCH's warranties and EMC's separate warranty appears in Section 8. Whether EMC is thereby made to give the Section 10 representations is a genuine question.

The clause lists three responses — "(i) cure such breach ..., (ii) purchase the affected Mortgage Loan ... or (iii) ... substitute" — without saying who elects among them, and then declares those obligations the "sole and exclusive remedy under this Agreement or otherwise." Whether the seller or the purchaser chooses, and how far "or otherwise" reaches, are both open on the words.

The remedy is confined to breaches affecting "MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans," while Section 10(a) makes MSMCH's warranties as to "each Mortgage Loan" in the pool. Breaches of Section 10(a) as to non-represented loans are left with no stated remedy.

The paragraph speaks of "a breach of a representation or warranty set forth in this Section 10 made by Accredited," but Accredited makes no representations in Section 10 — its warranties live in a separate assignment, assumption and recognition agreement. The trigger for MSMCH's backstop obligation is thus described inaccurately.

MSMCH's backstop runs to Accredited Mortgage Loans, but Accredited-originated loans fall outside the defined class of MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans to which the preceding remedy paragraph is limited. Whether the 90-day cure/purchase machinery applies to them at all must be construed.

The clause purports to fix when a cause of action "shall accrue" — on discovery or notice plus failure to cure or repurchase — which can be read either as a condition precedent to suit or as an attempt to postpone the running of limitations. That choice determines whether claims are timely and is not settled by the words.

Accrual is stated only "as to any MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loan," although the sentence opens by covering breaches of "any representations and warranties made in this Section 10," which under Section 10(a) reach each Mortgage Loan. The two halves of the sentence do not cover the same loans.

Sections 2(a), 2(c) and 20 all treat Section 11 as containing the conditions to closing, but Section 11 is an assignment of the Accredited agreement and the Fremont bring-down letter and states no conditions. The instrument cannot be read coherently until that mismatch is resolved.

The condition refers to Certificates sold "pursuant to the Underwriting Agreement and the Purchase Agreement," but "the Purchase Agreement" is not a defined term anywhere in this instrument. Which document is meant cannot be told from the text.

"EMC and MSMCH shall pay fees and expenses as previously agreed" identifies neither the fees nor the agreement fixing them, so the allocation of costs is indefinite on the face of the clause. Which expenses fall within it cannot be determined from the words.

The clause depends on a prior, unwritten arrangement, yet Section 29 declares this Agreement the entire agreement and "supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements ... oral or written." The two provisions pull in opposite directions.

The facsimile number given for EMC ("241-626-4714") is malformed and differs from the EMC fax number in the attached Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement, which could matter to whether notice was validly given.

The clause makes the Trustee's sole remedy "the cure, purchase or substitution obligations contained in Sections 5 and 7 hereof," but those obligations are in Section 10; Sections 5 and 7 are examination of mortgage files and EMC's corporate representations. It also preserves for the Purchaser benefits "set forth in Sections 12, 14 and 18," although Section 12 is reserved and Section 18 is a notice provision.

Termination rights are keyed to "the conditions ... set forth under Section 11(a)" and "Section 11(b)," but Section 11 has subsections (a) and (b) that assign two agreements and contain no closing conditions; the conditions are in Section 14(a) and (b). The termination right cannot be exercised as written without correcting the reference.

Section 26 obliges the parties to carry out "any amendments hereto which may be required by either Rating Agency," while this section forbids amendment without the prior written consent of each party. Whether a rating-agency-driven amendment can be compelled turns on reconciling the two.

The obligation to take actions "including any amendments hereto which may be required by either Rating Agency" sits against Section 24, which bars any amendment without each party's prior written consent. A party could read this section as compelling the very consent Section 24 makes optional.

The section extends the benefit of the Agreement to Bear Stearns "to the extent specified in Section 14 hereof," but Section 14 (conditions to closing) confers nothing on Bear Stearns; the provisions naming Bear Stearns are in Section 5(a). The extent of Bear Stearns' rights is therefore unascertainable from the reference given.

The clause supersedes all prior agreements on the subject matter, yet Section 15 makes the parties' fee obligations turn on terms "as previously agreed" and the Agreement elsewhere depends on the attached Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement. Whether those prior arrangements survive is a real question.

The enumeration is corrupted — item (ii) is followed by a second, unbracketed "ii)" — and item (v) reads "Verification of © acceptable evidence of source and amount of downpayment." The list of required file contents is not cleanly stated.

This exhibit defines the Mortgage File as containing only "copies of the Mortgage Loan Documents" and ancillary papers, while Section 4(b) requires delivery of original Mortgages, original assignments and, in lieu of original Mortgage Notes, lost note affidavits. What the seller actually had to deliver cannot be settled from the exhibit alone.

The closing sentence requires "the total of each of the amounts described under (0) above," but item (o) is the Interest Rate Adjustment Date, which is a date and cannot be totalled; the drafter plainly meant item (n), the principal balances. The aggregation requirement is unworkable as written.

This 25-item exhibit list differs from the 33-item definition of "Mortgage Loan Schedule" in Section 1, which Section 3 nevertheless equates with the Exhibit 2 information. The required contents of the schedule are stated twice and inconsistently.
